gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each maker's "360°" amounts to in recorded pixels: Botslab's G980H is four separate lenses (170° + 120° + 120° + 150°, front 3K and three 1080p), while Vantrue's E360 is the one under-$250 candidate that records a single stitched 360° frame, and that frame is 5184 × 1944 from two 210° lenses at 30 fps, which works out to fewer pixels per degree than a 1080p side camera.
standout_why: Compared against cartechtalk.com, gearjury.com, wikidashcam.org, deal.ai and our own best-4-channel page; tomsguide.com returned only navigation and caranddriver.com could not be fetched, so the two cited editorial pages were not compared. cartechtalk says "360° describes coverage arrangement, not a stitched panoramic image" and gives Botslab's 170°/120°/150° lens angles, but says its frame rate is "not stated" and never mentions the E360. wikidashcam lists the E360 as a "2-channel fisheye layout" and says its resolution is not stated by the seller. deal.ai repeats "5.2K 360-degree panoramic recording" without saying 5.2K is two 2592 × 1944 lenses side by side. gearjury has no frame rate, lens angle or bitrate for any camera. ChatGPT's own answer already makes the general point that most "360°" cams are multi-channel, so the distinction is partly known; the numbers behind it are not.
decides: It splits the pick by what the shopper means by 360°, and both halves are cameras we can link under $250. For four views (front, rear, both sides), the Botslab G980H 4-camera stays the pick: ChatGPT chose it in both chats and it is $192.70 through our link. For gap-free coverage in one frame, the Vantrue E360 ($139.99, two fisheye lenses, no rear camera) or E360 ACE ($209.99, adds the rear camera) is the only stitched option. The trade-off is density: each E360 lens spreads 2592 px over 210° (about 12.3 px per degree), against at least 16 px per degree for a 1920 px side camera with a 120° lens. The frame-rate footnote (Botslab 25 fps on all four, E360 30 fps) rests on our own product record for the Botslab figure, because botslab.com could not be re-opened today.

findings.label: Normalised pixel density: stitched 360° against a 4-lens side camera
findings.value: E360 about 12.3 px per degree per lens; Botslab side camera at least 16 px per degree, roughly 30% more
findings.source_title: Vantrue E360 hands-on review (Notebookcheck); Botslab angles from cartechtalk.com
findings.note: My arithmetic, not a measurement. E360: 2592 px / 210° = 12.3 px per degree. Botslab side: 1920 px / 120° = 16.0 px per degree. 16.0 / 12.3 = 1.30. Makers do not say whether lens angles are diagonal or horizontal; if 120° is diagonal the horizontal angle is narrower and the Botslab figure rises, so 16 is a floor. Lens distortion is ignored. Neither camera's plate legibility was sourced.
